highlights:
H100 price per hour on 3 November 2026: published rates from $1.99 to $9.80, a live index at $2.94, and what the hourly rate leaves out.

C Compute · H100 price per hour, per GPU Read 3 November 2026

$2.94 Silicon Data neocloud H100 index, per GPU-hour, 2 November 2026

Index and rate cards read 3 November 2026. The $3.90 median is Casitel OS, nine GPU clouds, 3 November 2026. Not executed prices.

The H100 price per hour depends on who you ask. On 2 November 2026 Silicon Data's neocloud H100 index read $2.94 per GPU-hour. Published on-demand rates read on 3 November ran from $1.99 to $9.80. Both numbers are real. They measure different things.

## What providers publish

A rate card is one provider's price for one configuration, on demand, with no commitment. These are the H100 lines on the providers' own pricing pages.

Provider Published H100 rate What the line says

Together AI$3.99 GPU clusters, on demand

RunPod, secure cloud$3.99 H100 SXM

DigitalOcean$4.41 GPU Droplet, on demand

Nebius$4.50 HGX H100, on demand

Fireworks AI$8.00 Dedicated H100

Google Cloud$9.80 Vertex AI H100, read 8 October 2026

Pages were read on 3 November 2026 unless a row says otherwise. Prices move. Nebius showed $3.85 on 8 October. It showed $4.50 on 3 November. Lambda lists $3.29 for a single PCIe GPU and $4.29 for a single SXM GPU, so even one provider has no single H100 price.

...

## Why the quote is not the contract

A rate card is for today, for one GPU, with no promise. A large buyer changes all three. Providers publish part of that change. Together lists $3.99 on demand, then $3.69 for 3 to 30 days, $3.45 for 31 to 90 days and $3.19 for 91 to 180 days. For longer terms it says to contact sales. DigitalOcean lists $3.26 for a 12-month H100 commitment against $4.41 on demand. Hyperstack lists reserved H100 SXM from $2.72 against $3.20 on demand.

These are still published rates. They are not what any buyer signed. Volume, prepayment, start date and place are settled in private contracts, and nobody publishes them. Casitel holds no executed prices to show you here, and this post does not guess at them. The list price is not the price explains how those deals close.

# Hyperstack

GPU VMs billed by the minute from NexGen Cloud, a UK company with data centres in Europe and North America

 Editor Sebastiaan Smits 

 Published 29 October 2026 Last reviewed 29 October 2026 How we review 

## Quick Overview

| Company | NexGen Cloud Limited (Hyperstack) |
| --- | --- |
| Category | GPU Cloud Providers |

| Founded | Not stated |

| Self-Hosting | No |
| Main Features | On-demand GPU VMs, reservation pricing, spot VMs, secure private cloud, on-demand Kubernetes, object storage, AI Studio, Terraform provider, Python and Go SDKs |
| Pricing | Public hourly list in US dollars, for example H100 SXM $3.20/h and H200 SXM $3.99/h on demand (checked 29 October 2026) |
| Best For | Developers who want short GPU sessions with minute-level billing and an English-law contract |
| Replaces | CoreWeave, Lambda, RunPod |

## Detailed Review

Hyperstack sells GPU capacity under the terms of NexGen Cloud Limited, which the terms page states are governed by the law of England and Wales. The pricing page lists billing accurate to the minute.

The GPU menu runs from L40 and RTX A6000 up to H100, H200, HGX B200 and B300, plus GB200 and GB300 NVL72 systems. A phone number with a London dialling code is printed in the header.

### Rates on the public list

On demand, the H100 PCIe is listed at $2.50 per hour, the H100 NVLink at $2.60 and the H100 SXM at $3.20, while A100 variants sit between $1.35 and $1.60. Reservation rates start lower, for example $1.75 for the H100 PCIe.

Every figure on the page is in US dollars and excludes whatever tax your country adds.

...

### Limitations to Consider

Data centres span Europe and North America, so residency depends on the region you select. Prices are quoted in US dollars. The pages checked do not name individual European sites, and a malicious look-alike domain was flagged by the vendor, so double-check the URL before signing up.

results.title: Hyperstack: GPU VM costs begin with the resource lifecycle — Retrivium
results.author: Retrivium team
highlights:
# Hyperstack: GPU VM costs begin with the resource lifecycle

Retrivium team Updated: 1 November 2026 2 min read Markdown ↓

THE QUICK TAKE

Know which states retain resources and charges. Verify the flavour, storage and completion procedure alongside model performance.

Hyperstack offers GPU VMs with selectable configurations and environments. A limited-budget team needs to understand creation, operation, stopping, data retention and deletion, not just rates. These actions can have different financial consequences.

This review uses official documentation as of 1 November 2026. It does not quote prices without specific account and resource conditions.

...

## Account for resource states

Resource Pricing explains charging and operations. Ordinary VM stopping does not necessarily release retained hardware and end billing. Preserved data has separate conditions.

The test plan must identify how the team ends the unwanted resource. Exiting a terminal or stopping the model process is not a substitute. Check data consequences and restoration before selecting the procedure.

## Budget the complete configuration

Public and account-applicable rates can differ by agreement. Preserve estimate date and resource composition. Include disks, networking, public addresses and other required components.

results.title: GPU cloud pricing: the list price is not the price | Casitel
highlights:
H100 rate cards ran from $1.99 to $9.80 a GPU-hour on 8 October 2026. Large buyers rarely pay them. How GPU deals close, and how to benchmark a quote.

C Compute · H100 list prices, per GPU-hour Rate cards read 8 October 2026

Range of published on-demand rates Median $3.90 $1.99$9.80

Each provider's own pricing page, read 8 October 2026. Not executed prices.

Every GPU cloud publishes a rate card. Few large buyers pay it. The rate card is where the negotiation starts, not where it ends.

## What the rate cards say

On 8 October 2026 the published on-demand rate for one Nvidia H100 ran from $1.99 to $9.80 an hour, across the providers that state a price per GPU.

Provider Published H100 rate What the rate covers

Voltage Park$1.99 From, bare metal

RunPod$1.99 From, secure cloud

GMI Cloud$2.60 From

Hyperstack$3.20 H100 SXM

Jarvislabs$3.49 H100 SXM

DataCrunch$3.85 H100 SXM5

Nebius$3.85 HGX H100

Crusoe$3.90 HGX H100

Lambda$3.99 H100 SXM, 8 GPUs

Together AI$3.99 HGX H100

Paperspace$5.95 H100

Fireworks AI$8.00 Dedicated H100

Google Cloud$9.80 Vertex AI H100

Each rate is the provider's own published figure, read from its pricing page on 8 October 2026. A rate marked "from" is the lowest tier on the page. Casitel OS reads these rate cards every day: on 3 November 2026 the median H100 list price across nine GPU clouds was $3.90 an hour.

...

A list price is for one GPU, today, with no commitment. A large deal changes every one of those terms.

- Term. A commitment of one year or more is priced below on-demand. DigitalOcean, for example, publishes $3.26 a GPU-hour for an H100 on a 12-month reservation.
- Volume. A cluster of thousands of GPUs is a different product from a single instance. The seller fills a whole hall at once.
- Payment. A deposit or prepayment buys a lower rate. It also moves risk from the seller to the buyer.
- Start date and place. Capacity that is live today costs more than capacity that goes live next year. A region with spare power costs less than one without.
- What is in the hour. Fast networking between GPUs, storage, support and data transfer are priced in some quotes and added on in others.

- The word "dedicated" covers everything from reserved slices of a shared pool to physically isolated clusters, so every evaluation should start by making each provider state which layers are shared with other customers.
- Isolation matters most at the GPU fabric, storage and compute layers, where neighbouring workloads cause both benchmark variance and slow InfoSec reviews.
- An SLA is only as credible as the standby hardware and support model behind it, and the consumption model decides how much of the stack your own team has to run.
- Hyperstack's Dedicated Cloud delivers single-tenant NVIDIA GPU clusters as GPU VMs through the same portal and API as its public-cloud regions, with the highest SLA of the four Secure Private Cloud tiers and a fixed monthly cost.

## 7. Price the Contract on Utilisation, Not on Hourly Rate

On a fixed contract of a year or longer, the hourly equivalent rate matters far less than the proportion of capacity your organisation actually uses, because idle GPUs cost the same as busy ones. Ask whether you can divide the cluster between departments, place workloads dynamically and repurpose idle capacity for research or spot-style jobs, since these capabilities turn one large commitment into a shared internal resource with a predictable cost per useful GPU-hour.

results.title: Four pricing changes in eight days at one provider. None at another. | Compute Stacker
results.author: Compute Stacker
highlights:
# Four pricing changes in eight days at one provider. None at another. | Compute Stacker · LinkedIn · 2026-10-27T00:00:00+00:00

**Compute Stacker**.

---

Four pricing changes in eight days at one provider. None at another.

What actually happened on H100 rate cards this month:

- October 1: Nebius raised on-demand H100 from $3.85 to $4.50, up 16.9%, and B300 from $7.85 to $9.50, up 21%. Its second increase in three months.
- October 7: AWS reserved Capacity Blocks moved to $5.970 per H100 accelerator-hour, the same rate across twelve regions.
- October 8: Nebius switched preemptible H100, H200, B200, B300 and RTX PRO 6000 to dynamic spot pricing. The published $2.15 became a floor of $0.79, with prices that can change every 15 minutes, including during a run, capped one cent below the on-demand rate.
- CoreWeave's HGX H100 node stayed at $49.24, or $6.16 per GPU.

Five things a headline rate doesn't tell you:

1. Per GPU or per node. CoreWeave, Oracle, Google and Azure sell H100s as 8-GPU nodes. If you need three, you pay for eight.
2. Volume rules. AWS charges $5.970 whether you take one GPU or eight. Lambda charges $4.29 for one and $3.99 each for eight.
3. Region. Nebius's H100 is in eu-north1 only. Google's 8-GPU H100 varies about 30% between its cheapest and priciest regions.
4. Purchase type. On-demand, spot, reserved and committed can differ by more than 3x on the same chip, with completely different reliability.
5. What's bundled. Lambda and CoreWeave list free egress. AWS charges about $0.09 per GB after an allowance.

The practical rule: compare the same purchase type, in the same region, at the same granularity, on the day you're buying. Anything else is comparing two different products.
